title: London in 7 Days: Pubs, Walking & Hidden Nightlife: South Bank → Soho → Shoreditch → Notting Hill → Greenwich → Camden → The City
description: A London adventure built for two who love walking, great pubs, and staying out late. Seven days to explore London's most rewarding neighborhoods on foot — iconic sights by day, legendary pubs and vibrant bars by night. From centuries-old taverns to craft beer railway arches, this is London for people who actually want to feel the city.

days.title: Arrival — South Bank, Westminster & First London Pints

activities.name: Westminster & Big Ben
activities.description: Get oriented — start at Westminster Tube and do the classic London arrival moment. Big Ben, Parliament, Westminster Bridge. Cross the bridge for a full river view with the London Eye ahead of you. Walk along the Thames from Westminster Bridge to Tate Modern — about 1.5km of London's finest riverside path. Pass the London Eye, Southbank Centre, National Theatre, and Globe Theatre on the way.
details: 📍 Westminster Tube (Jubilee/District/Circle lines)
💡 Pop into Tate Modern (free) for 30-60 min — the Turbine Hall alone is worth it.
tips: May in London means sunset around 8:45pm — you have long days. Don't rush the morning. The city reveals itself slowly.

activities.name: Borough Market
activities.description: London's greatest food market. Friday and Saturday it's fully open — all the legendary stalls. Padella pasta (queue moves fast), Kappacasein raclette, Bread Ahead doughnuts. Graze your way around rather than sitting down.
details: 📍 London Bridge Tube/rail · Open Mon-Sat
💡 Friday and Saturday are the biggest days. If you're here on a weekday, it's quieter but still open.

activities.name: Historic Pub Crawl: Bermondsey & Bankside
activities.description: Start your London pub education with two of the oldest and most atmospheric pubs in the city — both within a 5-minute walk of Borough Market.

activities.name: Dinner in Bermondsey
activities.description: Settle in for dinner after your pub warm-up. Bermondsey has quietly become one of London's best dining streets.
tips: José has no reservations and fills up fast. Arrive at 6pm or 8:30pm for the best chance of space. Worth the wait.

days.neighborhoods: City of London · Fleet Street · Covent Garden · Soho
days.title: The City, Fleet Street Pubs & Soho Night Out

activities.name: St Paul's Cathedral Walk
activities.description: The exterior of Wren's masterpiece is free to admire and photograph from everywhere. For the dome climb (365 steps, incredible city views), entry is £22pp. Walk around the cathedral and through the churchyard. Walk west from St Paul's through the medieval Inns of Court — the Temple (Middle and Inner Temple), Gray's Inn Gardens. These legal chambers have barely changed in 400 years. Free to walk through on weekdays.
details: 💡 The Whispering Gallery inside the dome is remarkable. Budget 1.5-2 hours if going inside.
💡 It feels like a time warp. The gardens at Middle Temple are open and beautiful in May.

activities.name: Fleet Street Historic Pub Walk
activities.description: Fleet Street — London's old newspaper row — has several of the city's most ancient pubs. Walk the short stretch between Chancery Lane and Blackfriars Tube, stopping in at the greats. Walk west to Covent Garden for the street performers in the piazza, the Apple Market, and window shopping. The Royal Opera House lobby is free to walk through.

activities.name: Soho Dinner & Bar Hop
activities.description: Head to Soho for London's best dinner and bar scene — dense, walkable, and endlessly entertaining. Wander Dean Street, Frith Street, and Old Compton Street.

activities.name: Soho Pub Crawl
activities.description: Three legendary Soho pubs in a 10-minute walk.
details: The French House, 49 Dean Street — half pints only (house rule), incredible Soho history, De Gaulle and Dylan Thomas drank here. A London institution.
The Dog and Duck, 18 Bateman Street — beautiful Victorian pub, Orwell allegedly drank here.
Bar Termini, 7 Old Compton Street — tiny Italian bar with some of London's best negronis.
tips: The French House serves only half pints — the landlord's rule since forever. They also have natural wines and genuinely good cheese. The whole pub is about 30 people max. It's a treasure.

days.neighborhoods: Spitalfields · Brick Lane · Shoreditch · Bethnal Green
days.title: East End & Shoreditch — Street Art, Spitalfields & Late Nights

activities.name: Spitalfields Market
activities.description: Start at this covered Victorian market. Sundays are the big day, but weekdays have food stalls, vintage shops, and good coffee. Great for browsing before heading deeper into the East End. Walk north up Brick Lane — the entire area is an open-air street art gallery. Turn onto Hanbury Street, Princelet Street, and the Shoreditch Triangle for the best murals. Artists like Banksy, ROA, and Stik have worked here.
details: 📍 Commercial Street, E1 · Liverpool Street Tube
💡 Download the Shoreditch Street Art map from Google 'Shoreditch street art tour' — it's well-documented.

activities.name: Sky Garden
activities.description: The 'Walkie Talkie' building's free rooftop garden gives 360° views over London. Must book free tickets online (skygarden.london) — they release 3 weeks ahead and go fast. 2-3pm is a great slot. Walk the Shoreditch Triangle: Rivington Street, Charlotte Road, Old Street. Street art walls everywhere. Boxpark has food from all over the world in converted shipping containers.
details: 💡 Free tickets at skygarden.london. If full, the Rooftop Bar at Montcalm Royal London House (nearby) has similar views for the cost of a drink.

activities.name: Craft Beer: Bethnal Green & Shoreditch
activities.description: London has an incredible craft beer scene concentrated in East London railway arches. Walk the Bethnal Green arches for some of the best.
details: Redchurch Brewery Taproom — local Shoreditch brewery, excellent pale ales
Beavertown Tottenham (nearby) — one of London's most famous craft breweries
EBF (East Beverley Follick) — tiny local, worth finding

activities.name: Shoreditch Bar Crawl
activities.description: London's best nightlife concentration for adventurous drinkers.
details: Happiness Forgets, Holywell Lane — basement speakeasy with exceptional cocktails. Book a table or arrive before 8pm. London's best cocktail bar many years running.
Discount Suit Company, Middlesex St — bar hidden inside what looks like a suit shop entrance. Creative cocktails, cool crowd.
XOYO, Cowper St — if you want a proper club night, this is Shoreditch's best. Check listings for the night.
tips: End the night at Beigel Bake (open 24 hours) — a salt beef bagel at 2am on Brick Lane is a London rite of passage.

days.title: Tower of London, Bermondsey Beer Mile & Thames Path Walk

activities.name: Tower of London
activities.description: Arrive at opening (10am) to beat crowds. Join a free Yeoman Warder (Beefeater) tour — they're dark, funny, and brilliantly knowledgeable. See the Crown Jewels (allow 30-45 min queue), the White Tower, and the spot where Anne Boleyn was executed. Cross Tower Bridge — it's free and the views are superb. The glass floor walkway costs £12pp if you want the vertigo experience. Walk over and back.
details: 💡 £33pp — prebook on the HRP website for timed entry. Allow 2.5-3 hours.
📍 Tower Hill Tube (Circle/District lines)
tips: The Beefeater tours are the highlight of the Tower. They're hilarious, dark, and completely compelling. Don't skip it — join the first tour of the day.

activities.name: Bermondsey Beer Mile Walk
activities.description: Walk south from Tower Bridge into Bermondsey — London's craft brewery district, crammed into Victorian railway arches. A 1km stretch with 10+ craft breweries, all open on weekends and most on weekday afternoons. Just a short walk from the Beer Mile — this is the locals' answer to Borough Market. Food stalls under railway arches, less touristy, equally delicious. Perfect late lunch while drinking.
details: Fourpure Brewing — great session IPAs and pilsners
Brew By Numbers — some of London's most experimental beers
Anspach & Hobday — the Smoked Porter alone is worth the trip
Partizan Brewing — excellent seasonals

activities.name: Thames Path: Shad Thames to Southwark
activities.description: Walk the Shad Thames riverside path — Victorian warehouse conversions with external walkways, mooring bollards, and stunning river views. One of London's most beautiful walks at golden hour.

activities.name: Borough Market Late Drinks
activities.description: Head back to Borough Market area — a cluster of excellent bars within a five-minute walk.
details: Rake Bar — tiny, legendary craft beer bar right in Borough Market. Excellent selection.
Brew Dog London Bridge — larger, reliably good craft beer selection.
Hide Bar — cocktails on Bermondsey Street, elegant and affordable.

days.neighborhoods: Notting Hill · Hyde Park · Camden Town
days.title: Notting Hill Walk & Camden Nightlife

activities.name: Notting Hill Walk
activities.description: Explore London's most photogenic neighborhood at a leisurely pace. The pastel-painted terraces on Portobello Road, Elgin Crescent, and Lancaster Road are at their best in May morning light. One of the world's great markets — antiques, vintage clothing, food stalls, and jewelry. Saturday is biggest, but Tuesday-Friday still has most shops open and is much less crowded.
details: 📍 Notting Hill Gate Tube (Central/Circle/District lines)
💡 Best for: vintage clothing (the covered section at Golborne Road end), antique silver and maps, and artisan food at the top end.
tips: The best Notting Hill photo streets: the blue houses on Portobello Road, the pastel terrace on St Luke's Mews (tiny, easy to miss), and the view down Ladbroke Grove from Holland Park Tube.

activities.name: Churchill Arms Pub Stop
activities.description: The most photographed pub in London — absolutely draped in flower baskets and plants, especially in May bloom. Even if just for one pint in the flower-covered facade, it's unmissable. The Thai restaurant in the back is also genuinely good. Walk southeast through Hyde Park — 350 acres of London's finest parkland. In May it's spectacular. See the Serpentine lake, the Diana Memorial Fountain, and cut through to Marble Arch.
details: 📍 119 Kensington Church St · Walk from Notting Hill
💡 The whole Notting Hill → Hyde Park → Camden route is about 8km but completely walkable through leafy streets.

activities.name: Camden Town
activities.description: Take the Tube to Camden Town — London's most chaotic, creative, and uniquely irreverent neighborhood. The Lock Market, the Canal, and the entire strip is unlike anywhere else.
details: 📍 Camden Town Tube (Northern line)

activities.name: Camden Music Venues & Bars
activities.description: Camden is London's live music heartland. Legendary venues within 200 metres of each other.
details: Jazz Café — world music, soul, funk. Great intimate venue.
Electric Ballroom — classic rock, indie, club nights. Been going since 1938.
Proud Camden — converted horse hospital with a rooftop bar and live acts.
The World's End — enormous Wetherspoon's pub right by the Tube. Cheap pints, no-frills, always packed.
tips: Check Dice FM or Resident Advisor for what's on at Camden venues. The Jazz Café often has excellent acts and an electric atmosphere. Book ahead if there's someone good on.

days.title: Greenwich & Brixton — History, Food & Late-Night Vibes

activities.name: Thames Clipper to Greenwich
activities.description: Take the river bus from Embankment or London Bridge pier — sit on the top deck for the best views of London from the water. 30-40 minutes of Thames scenery. Start with the beautifully restored Cutty Sark — the legendary tea clipper. Then walk through Greenwich Market (covered, great food stalls) for breakfast.
details: 💡 Oyster cards and contactless work on Thames Clippers. Get a return or a day pass.
📍 Cutty Sark DLR station

activities.name: Royal Observatory & Prime Meridian
activities.description: Climb the steep hill through Greenwich Park to the Royal Observatory. Stand on the Prime Meridian — 0° longitude — with one foot in each hemisphere. The views from the hilltop over the Cutty Sark, Queen's House, and Canary Wharf are iconic. Spread out in the park — in May the wildflower meadows and rose garden are in bloom. One of London's most peaceful places on a sunny afternoon.
details: 💡 The park and Prime Meridian photo (outside the Observatory) are free. £18pp to go inside. The view from the hill is magnificent either way.

activities.name: Brixton — London's Most Vibrant Neighborhood
activities.description: Take the Overground or Tube to Brixton — London's most electric neighborhood for food and nightlife. The market, the restaurants, and the bar scene are all exceptional.
details: 📍 Brixton Tube (Victoria line) · 20 min from central London
tips: Franco Manca original site in Brixton Village makes the best sourdough pizza in London. The queue is always worth it. Get the No. 2 with buffalo mozzarella.

activities.name: Brixton Nightlife
activities.description: Brixton has London's best nightlife concentration outside of central London — and a better atmosphere than most of Zone 1.
details: Dogstar — legendary Brixton pub-turned-club, great drinks and later a DJ. Always busy.
NMT (Never Mind the Bollocks) — Brixton's best pub for music and local crowd.
Electric Brixton — 1,500-cap venue with the best sound system in south London.
Phonox — intimate techno and house club. One of London's finest small clubs.
tips: Brixton feels like the real London that tourists don't usually reach. The music at Phonox or Electric Brixton is world-class. Book tickets in advance.

days.neighborhoods: Bethnal Green · Islington · Angel · King's Cross
days.title: Columbia Road Market, Canals & Farewell London Pints

activities.name: Columbia Road Flower Market
activities.description: One of London's most extraordinary experiences — Sunday only, 8am-2pm. A narrow East End street transforms into a riot of flowers and color. Traders call out in Cockney rhyming slang, everyone carries armfuls of blooms. Go between 9-11am before it gets packed.
details: 📍 Columbia Road E2 · Bus or Overground to Hoxton/Bethnal Green
💡 Sunday ONLY. Arrive by 9am for the best experience. Extremely photogenic.

activities.name: Regent's Canal Walk
activities.description: Walk along the Regent's Canal from Islington west toward King's Cross. One of London's most pleasant walking routes — narrowboats, towpaths, and a completely different pace of city. About 3km to King's Cross. A detour through Clerkenwell — one of London's most underrated neighborhoods. Exmouth Market is a pedestrianized street with excellent lunch spots. The area has brilliant gastropubs.
details: 💡 Pick up the canal at Angel (City Road Basin) and walk west. You'll pass through the tunnel at Islington (boats go through, walkers climb over the hill) and emerge at King's Cross Basin.

activities.name: Farewell Pub Crawl: Islington to Angel
activities.description: Islington has a brilliant cluster of old pubs for your final London evening.
tips: The Compton Arms is easy to miss — look for the tiny sign on Compton Avenue off Canonbury Road. It's one of those pubs that makes you understand why people love London.

activities.name: Last London Walk
activities.description: Walk or Tube back to your hotel area. If you have time, take one last Thames walk — the South Bank at night, with St Paul's lit across the water and the Shard glowing, is London at its most beautiful.
details: 💡 London is never really finished. But if seven days of walking, great pubs, brilliant food, and late nights haven't made you want to move here — nothing will.
tips: Look out your last London train or Tube window as you head to the airport. The city is extraordinary. Come back.
